intro: College teachers of education already train future teachers, plan curriculum and run research. The closest of the 25 careers below is Instructional Coordinators, with a 92% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $77,440, which is 3% more than the $75,350 education teachers in higher education earn.
why_it_works: Teaching teachers means explaining methods, observing classrooms and turning research into practice. O*NET rates instructing at 4.12 out of 5 for this job and complex problem solving at 3.75. Curriculum, adult education and administration roles use those skills every day. All 25 matches need no new degree. The gaps are coordinating people across a district and day-to-day service work.
tips: Lead a curriculum review or accreditation project now; it is direct proof for coordinator and administrator jobs.
Postsecondary education administrators earn $104,590, which is 39% more, and are an 82% match.
If you enjoy research on people at work, look at organizational psychology, the best-paid match.

faq.q: What jobs can former education professors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Instructional Coordinators (92%), secondary special education teachers (84%) and adult basic education and ESL instructors (83%), based on O*NET 31.0. Postsecondary education administrators are also 82% matched and earn $104,590, which is 39% more than the $75,350 median.

faq.q: Which careers for education professors pay more?
faq.a: 7 of the 25 matches pay more. Industrial-Organizational Psychologists earn $193,950 (157% more), Sociologists $106,030 (41% more) and school administrators below the college level $105,870 (41% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Psychology roles usually need specific graduate training in that field.

faq.q: Do education professors need another degree?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than postsecondary education teachers already have. A master's degree is the most common level, held by 60% of workers in the closest match, so your existing degree usually covers the move.

faq.q: What skills should education professors build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are coordination, service orientation, operations monitoring and social perceptiveness. Time management already rates 3.5 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so managing programs, budgets and staff is the main step toward coordinator or dean roles.
